narrative:
The decision regarding your law school application was influenced by a prediction indicating a 70.6% chance that you would fail the bar exam if you were to take it. This high probability of failure is a significant concern for admissions committees, as passing the bar is crucial for a successful legal career.

The primary factors contributing to this prediction were your academic performance in your first and third years, as well as your undergraduate GPA. Your rankings in both your first and third years placed you in the lowest decile compared to accepted students, who typically ranked much higher. This suggests that your academic performance may not have met the expectations set by the school for successful bar exam candidates.

Additionally, your undergraduate GPA of 3.10 is below the average of 3.23 among accepted students, further indicating potential challenges in mastering the material necessary for passing the bar exam. While your family income bracket and full-time work status were not directly influencing factors in this prediction, they can impact the resources and support available to you during your studies.

To improve your chances for future applications, consider focusing on enhancing your academic performance, particularly in your remaining coursework, and seek opportunities to strengthen your study skills and bar exam preparation. Engaging in preparatory courses or seeking mentorship from successful law students may also provide valuable insights and support.
